The Tashahhud the Prophet taught instead of 'peace be on Allah', who is As-Salam, and supplications in prayer: refuge from the grave, the Dajjal, sin and debt, and forgiveness.
Mud marked the Prophet's forehead from prostrating; followers said the Taslim together with him, as at Itban's house, and he stayed seated while the women left.
After compulsory prayers Allah was praised aloud; the poor are told to say Subhan Allah, Al-hamdu lillah and Allahu Akbar thirty-three times each; the Prophet's words of Allah's oneness.
After the Taslim the Prophet faced the people, once relaying Allah's words on crediting rain to stars; he waited for women to leave and once hurried to give away gold.
Whoever eats garlic or onion should keep away from the mosque; the Prophet declined a pot of strong-smelling vegetables, saying he converses with those they do not.
A man who passed a grave set apart from the others with the Prophet said the Prophet led the people in the funeral prayer, with them aligned behind him.
An orphan stood with Anas behind the Prophet; young Ibn Abbas joined the rows and the Eid; Friday bathing binds those past puberty; Isha was delayed till children slept.
Men should not stop women going to the mosque, even at night; women left first after the Taslim, unrecognised in Fajr's dark; Umm Sulaim stood behind Anas and an orphan.
Friday, which earlier nations differed over, was given to this nation; whoever attends should bathe, use siwak and perfume, come early and listen silently, his sins since last Friday forgiven.
Umar urged a silk cloak on the Prophet for Fridays; he said it is worn by one with no share in the Hereafter; Umar gave his to a pagan brother.
The Prophet would have ordered the siwak for every prayer but for the hardship, urged it repeatedly, cleaned his mouth at night, and used a siwak Aisha chewed for him.
The Prophet recited As-Sajda and Ad-Dahr in Friday's Fajr; the next Jumua after his mosque's was at Jawathi in Bahrain; a governor is told to lead Jumua, all being guardians.
Whoever comes to Jumua should bathe, a duty on all past puberty; Friday was given to this nation after others differed, and every Muslim should bathe once in seven days.
Women should be allowed to mosques at night; a wife of Umar kept praying Fajr and Isha there, as the Prophet forbade stopping Allah's women-slaves from Allah's mosques.
On a muddy day Ibn Abbas had people pray at home though Jumua is compulsory; bathing was urged on workers arriving dusty and sweaty; Jumua was prayed soon after midday.
Feet dusty in Allah's cause are saved from Hell; walk calmly to the prayer; whoever bathes and does not push between two people is forgiven; none may unseat another.
The Friday Adhan was called once the imam sat on the pulpit, until Uthman added one at Az-Zawra; Muawiya repeated the Adhan's words from the pulpit, as the Prophet did.
An Ansari woman's slave carpenter made the pulpit of tamarisk; the Prophet prayed on it to teach, the palm stem he stood by cried, and he preached standing, sitting between.
After the eclipse prayer the Prophet said 'Amma ba'du' and told that he had seen Paradise and Hell and that people will be tried in their graves, asked about him.
The Prophet opened addresses with the Tashahhud, praise and 'Amma ba'du', as when explaining why he gave to some and not others, and why he stopped leading the night prayer.
In his last gathering, from the pulpit, the Prophet said the Ansar will decrease, and any ruler should accept the good among them and overlook their wrongdoers' faults.
The Prophet gave two sermons, sitting between them; angels record Friday arrivals by the hour, then listen; a man entering during the sermon is told to pray two rak'at.
In a Friday sermon the Prophet prayed for rain at a man's request; it rained a week until a man asked again, and the Prophet prayed it away from Medina.
Telling a companion to be quiet during the sermon is wrong; Friday holds a short hour when requests are granted; people left for a food caravan, and a verse came.
The Prophet prayed two rak'at before and after Zuhr and after Maghrib and Isha, and after Jumua prayed two rak'at only once he was home.
After Jumua the companions ate a woman's dish of silq roots and barley, looking forward to Friday; they napped and ate only after the Jumua prayer, which was prayed early.
Facing the enemy, the Prophet led the fear prayer in two parties, one praying with him while the other stood guard, then changing; if outnumbered, pray standing or riding.
On the day of the Trench neither Umar nor the Prophet had prayed Asr before sunset; the Prophet made ablution at Buthan and prayed Asr, then Maghrib.
Returning from the Confederates, the Prophet said to pray Asr only at Bani Quraiza; some delayed it, others prayed on the way, and he blamed neither group.
After praying Fajr in the dark the Prophet rode on Khaybar; its fighters were killed, women and children taken captive, and he married Safiya, her freedom being her dowry.
Umar urged a silk cloak on the Prophet for Eid; he said it is for those with no share in the Hereafter, then later sent Umar one to sell.
On Eid the Prophet told Abu Bakr to leave two girls singing songs of Bu'ath, and let Aisha watch, standing behind him, as Bani Arfida played with shields and spears.
On Eid al-Adha the first act is the prayer and the sacrifice comes after returning from it; whoever does so follows the Prophet's way.
When Abu Bakr objected to two Ansari girls singing on Eid, the Prophet said every nation has its Eid; he ate an odd number of dates before Eid al-Fitr prayer.
A sacrifice slaughtered before the Eid prayer must be repeated, being only meat; the Prophet let Abu Burda offer a young she-goat instead, valid for him alone.
On both Eids the Prophet prayed first, without Adhan, then preached and went to the women for alms; Abu Sa'id protested when Marwan gave the sermon before the prayer.
The Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman prayed the Eid prayer before the sermon, without adhan; the Prophet then preached to the women, who gave their jewellery as alms.
On Eid the prayer comes first and the sacrifice after; an animal slaughtered before the prayer is only meat, and the Prophet allowed Abu Burda alone a young goat instead.
Wounded by a spearhead at Mina, Ibn Umar told Al-Hajjaj he was to blame, for allowing arms to be carried on a day they never were and inside the Haram.
In his Nahr sermon the Prophet said the prayer comes before slaughtering, a sacrifice before it is only meat, and Abu Burda alone could offer a young goat instead.
